chunks: My relation with the Messenger of Allah is that of one branch with another, or of the wrist with the forearm.

By Allah, if the Arabs join together to fight me I will not run away from them and if I get the opportunity I will hasten to catch them by their necks. I shall surely strive to relieve the earth of this man of perverse mind and uncouth body, till the bits of earth are removed from the grain.

key_terms.الشَّخْصِ الْمَعْكُوسِ: The person with a twisted or perverse mind/character.
key_terms.الصِّنْوِ: A branch or shoot from a tree, used here to denote close kinship.
key_terms.الْجِسْمِ الْمَرْكُوسِ: The body that is rough or uncouth.

ai.seo_question: What metaphor does the Imam use to describe his relationship with the Prophet Muhammad in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) employs the metaphor of 'the branch from the branch' to assert his inseparable spiritual and political continuity with the Prophet, emphasizing his authority to act as the Prophet's direct representative. He specifically targets the 'corrupt leader'—widely interpreted by Shia scholars as Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan—vowing to eradicate him to purify the earth of tyranny, thereby linking his governance to the purification of the community from Umayyad influence.
